academicJudgment.claim: The confirmed global politics and empirical-methods core supports two meaningful broader UCR responses, while the revised-cohort final-year theory and research culmination remains outside the assessed scope.
academicJudgment.basis: Actual comparative politics, political theory, international relations, public/international law and quantitative/qualitative inquiry supply sustained political substance. The first option adds political economy/public governance; the second adds actual conflict, war/empire, criminal-justice/radicalisation and data inquiry, while retaining core international politics.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: General law/economics/communication coherence would not suffice. Both options retain multiple actual political/institutional courses and empirical methods; contextual breadth has specific roles. Missing dedicated political projects and research culmination remain major limitations and are not disguised as optional research. The historical research course remains American/historical and radicalisation prevention supplies its actual psychosocial contribution.
